milestone: Iterator25: pending THROW retains a by-reference foreach wrapper
status: Implemented, validated and independently accepted; pointwise composed over f63bef869/401.
scope: A one-Throwable literal throw method call on a pending actual Generator follows finite pure native links to a bare statement yield inside exactly one active by-reference array foreach with a simple-CV item target. No buffered input or other owning suspended task/HELD value, inactive GC; getters and explicit close only, no later real resume.
semantics: The acquired foreach count belongs to the actual reference wrapper, not a frozen array snapshot. The item CV aliases an embedded entry cell and contributes a separate count. Pending THROW preserves both until physical close, without body entry or a persistent exception owner in the parked Generator.

Physical close transfers the acquired HCELL task count to existing request retention, removes the iterator, and retires the item CV normally. Whole-wrapper replacement can release the old array and its elements; the new value remains reachable through the retained wrapper. An escaped-item write instead changes its actual entry cell.

Copied-current cleanup remains separate: a genuine cache destructor after receiver close can replace the injected Throwable while retaining its previous chain. Request-store payload destruction leaves the retained wrapper count in the terminal state. No new state field, root representation, collector algorithm or ordinary iteration-advance rule is introduced.
source_authority: vendor/php-src/Zend/zend_generators.c::Generator::throw, zend_generator_resume, zend_generator_dtor_storage and zend_generator_close: pending THROW parks before HANDLE_EXCEPTION, while close follows the parked unfinished-execution history.

Zend/zend_vm_def.h::FE_RESET_RW and FE_FETCH_RW retain the acquired reference wrapper and alias the visited entry into the item CV. Zend/zend_execute.c::cleanup_live_vars normally releases a LOOP owner; the observed parked close misses that live range, retaining the mutable wrapper rather than immutable element pins.
Pinned implementation observations are not portable evaluation-order guarantees. No engine bug or intentional divergence is classified.
